rule: Each entry names something the spine used to invent. A standard is adopted for what it actually covers and for nothing else; what it does NOT do is recorded beside it so the adoption is not read as a guarantee.

standards.name: OWASP CycloneDX, ECMA-424
standards.replaces: the ad-hoc BoM CSV invented in core.bom
standards.covers: HBOM for physical parts (component type 'device'), OBOM for the runtime configuration, MBOM for what a lab is assembled from; CDXA for attestations
standards.does_not: it does not price anything. Provenance of a price stays this estate's problem.
standards.ties_to: in-toto predicate type https://cyclonedx.org/bom — the same in-toto Statement v1 the Candor receipts already use

standards.name: Development Containers Specification
standards.replaces: a bespoke 'how to start this lab' README step
standards.covers: one file that VS Code, Codespaces, DevPod, Coder and the devcontainer CLI all read; hostRequirements states the RAM, CPU and storage the lab needs
standards.does_not: it does not provision hardware, and it is not a multi-container orchestrator — compose is still referenced for that.

standards.name: RO-Crate
standards.replaces: an evidence folder whose contents only a human could interpret
standards.covers: ro-crate-metadata.json, JSON-LD over schema.org: what was captured, by what instrument, when, by whom, under what licence
standards.does_not: it asserts nothing about whether the measurement is correct.
standards.ties_to: the evidence requirement in D4 and in every lab kit

standards.name: Technology Readiness Levels, ISO 16290:2013
standards.replaces: nothing — the five-rung ladder stays. This is a DECLARED MAPPING so a collaborator can state a TRL to a funder without inventing one
standards.covers: the nine-level maturity scale ESA, NASA, the US DoD and Horizon Europe all read
standards.does_not: a rung does not compute a TRL. The mapping gives a RANGE, and the assessment itself is left to the adopting organisation, exactly as ISO 16290 leaves it.

standards.name: Unified Code for Units of Measure
standards.replaces: free-text units in conformance conditions ('Hz and Hz/s', 'microseconds')
standards.covers: machine-readable unit codes, prefixes, and {annotation} syntax for dimensionless quantities
standards.does_not: it carries no ontology; QUDT is where a unit links to its quantity kind.
standards.ties_to: D4 — a criterion with no unit is not a criterion
